mission: Aelia steps down in public disgrace to preserve the Foundation’s legitimate charitable work. Korda is the official dead fall guy.
why_now: The Iresh operation’s collapse became public, and someone — Tess, or whoever is cleaning the board — has already written Korda as the rogue center. Aelia is stepping down to protect the Foundation’s legitimate work before the inquiry can reach the Vigil’s inner ring.
conflict: Ben watches a woman who genuinely helped grieving families deliver the most controlled and effective public lie he has ever seen — framed not as a lie but as accountability, civic responsibility, and grief. The Foundation will survive. Aelia chose that. Ben knows everything she is not saying.
turning_point: Ben knows the public story is incomplete.
closing_hook: Ben knows the public story is incomplete.
setting: Coruscant, the Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation building during a press conference. The atrium is full of newsfeed projectors and grieving family-member spokespeople. Aelia Vandros at a podium, announcing her resignation in a measured, civic register. Korda named as the rogue center of the scandal. Ben watches from the side, civilian-dressed. The Foundation's name-wall behind Aelia lists the war dead the charity has always genuinely served: Second Galactic Civil War casualties, Yuuzhan Vong War dead, and the names from the Battle of Shedu Maad that gave the Foundation its name. That wall is real. The grief in the room is real. The lie is real inside both.

stakes.personal: Ben is watching the public version of the case he lived — and it is clean, competent, and almost entirely wrong. He cannot stand up and correct it. He cannot hand them Iressa's destroyed reconstruction, or Talon's testimony, or Tess's fingerprints. He has the container in his belt and the knowledge of what the Vigil was actually doing and no clean way to say any of it without burning things he does not want to burn.
stakes.interpersonal: Aelia looks at Ben once across the atrium — a brief, controlled recognition. She is not asking him to say nothing. She already knows he cannot say the right thing in the right place at the right time. She built the situation so that is the case.
stakes.external: The public story is already calcifying. Every grief family in the room believes Korda was the rogue element. The Foundation will survive. The Vigil's ideology and method survive inside an institution people need. The wrong that Ben came to correct is not corrected — it is contained.

sensory_details: The Foundation atrium under newsfeed light: a projection-lit podium, rows of grieving family spokespeople arranged in a way that reads as witness rather than staging, the Foundation's memorial name-wall visible through the glass partition behind Aelia. The Candle Room is locked behind a plain marker. Ben is civilian-dressed, standing near the back, and at least three people have clocked him and are carefully not looking again. One concrete anchor: the name-wall. It runs three columns — Yuuzhan Vong War, Second Galactic Civil War, Shedu Maad — and the names are engraved, not projected. Families paid to have them there. That is the thing Ben cannot argue with from the back of the room: the Foundation was genuinely needed, and the names on that wall are genuinely dead.

turning_point_detail.trigger: Aelia's press conference ends. She has named Korda as the rogue element, announced her resignation as an act of responsibility rather than guilt, and done it in a register that made the grieving families feel protected and witnessed rather than manipulated.
turning_point_detail.shift: Ben understands she has won. Not morally — the Vigil's ideology survives inside the Foundation, Tess survives, the One Sith purpose survives — but operationally. The public story is set. The inquiry will find Korda's body at the center and stop there.
turning_point_detail.cost: Ben knows the story is incomplete. He cannot prove how incomplete. The truth lives in a destroyed secondary cache, a dead manifest analyst, and an unfinished holocron in his belt pouch — none of which he can bring into the open without explaining things he has decided not to explain.

emotional_arc.start: Ben arrives at the press conference to see what the public version looks like — partly reconnaissance, partly something harder to name, like needing to watch the official ending even knowing it is wrong.
emotional_arc.shift: Aelia's brief look across the atrium confirms they both know what this is. She is not deceived about what Ben knows. She is betting correctly that he cannot use it.
emotional_arc.end: Ben leaves before the press conference ends. He knows the public story is incomplete. The knowledge is not satisfying. It is just something he has to carry.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben watches Aelia's press conference from the civilian back of the atrium — civilian-dressed, avoiding eye contact, reading the staging as he watches it work on the room.
key_beats.state_change: He sees the official version of the case being installed in real time, in front of people who have legitimate grief.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the specific flatness of watching a lie that contains real things; no way to name it without destroying something else

key_beats.beat_description: Aelia delivers the official story: Korda as the rogue center, her resignation as civic responsibility, the Foundation's legitimate charitable work protected by her departure.
key_beats.state_change: The public narrative is set — Korda takes the center, Aelia takes the civic exit, and the Vigil's inner ring is untouched.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the recognition of a well-built structure; no obvious seam to pull; the frustration of watching something competent that is wrong

key_beats.beat_description: The grief families in the room receive it as real, because the Foundation's public work was real and Aelia's warmth for it is real.
key_beats.state_change: The lie is not purely a lie — the charitable work it protects was genuine, and that genuineness makes the official story stickier than propaganda.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the discomfort of watching people comforted by something incomplete; the knowledge that he cannot offer them the alternative

key_beats.beat_description: Aelia meets Ben's gaze once across the atrium — recognition, not apology, not threat.
key_beats.state_change: She has confirmed she knows he knows, and that she has correctly bet he cannot deploy that knowledge from here.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the look received without surprise; the acknowledgment of being correctly assessed by someone across the room

key_beats.beat_description: Ben leaves before the press conference ends; the public story is already calcifying and he cannot correct it.
key_beats.state_change: The case is operationally resolved and morally unresolved simultaneously — the wrong is contained, not corrected.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the knowledge settling as something to carry rather than solve; the exit before the room applauds

canon_elements_needed: Second Galactic Civil War war dead: the Foundation's legitimate charitable mandate began here; the name-wall carries these casualties
Yuuzhan Vong War dead: the Foundation's oldest named grief cohort; listed first on the name-wall by date
Battle of Shedu Maad: the Foundation's namesake engagement; the final column on the name-wall; the loss that gave the charity its credibility and its cover simultaneously
